dim_resolution.action: scan country_code dict to find us_code; build bitset of cn_id with country_code != 0 AND != us_code; also keep direct pointer to name.off/name.dat for MIN projection
scan info varlen twice for 'countries' (it1_id) and 'rating' (it2_id)
scan keyword.off/.dat for {murder, murder-in-title, blood, violence}; collect kw_ids
scan kind for {movie, episode}; build kt_ids

filters.predicate: note non-empty AND NOT memmem(note,'(USA)') AND memmem(note,'(200')

join_order.notes: Cheapest semi-join first; mk has ~4.5M rows but kw_ids selectivity is very high; semi-break on first match
Must collect MIN(mi_idx.info) over all matching rows; do not break early — track running min within and across rows

Check note LIKE filters (two memmem), then test non_us_cn_bitset[company_id]. ct join is trivial (any ct.id 1..4 matches). Track running MIN(cn.name) by indexing name.off/name.dat at company_id. Must find at least one match for v to qualify.

data_structures.kw_ids: flat_hash_set<int32_t> (size 4) or sorted small array with linear scan
data_structures.running_min: three string_view holders (best_cn_name, best_mi_idx_info, best_t_title) compared via lex order across surviving v

parallelism.reduction: per-thread running mins (3 string_views), final reduce by lex-min

notes: Same shape as Q22a; only the production_year cutoff tightens from >2008 to >2009 — fewer driver survivors.
Probe ordering: mk (cheapest filter, semi-break) -> mi_idx (must enumerate for MIN) -> mi (semi-break) -> mc (must enumerate for cn MIN).
All semi-join probes break on first qualifying row to minimize work.
For mi_idx and mc, the row must produce at least one match AND we must scan all matches to update running MIN projections — do not break early on these.
Resolve us_code via dict scan once; encode company_name.country_code filter as a 234997-bit bitset (~29 KB, fits L1).
No external hash join: all dim sides are tiny (sets of size ≤4) or single-bit lookups.
